newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says shorter stock settlement on Aug 18.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says shorter stock settlement on Aug 18.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) will begin implementing a shorter stock settlement period of "T-plus-5" on August 18, KLSE executive chairman Nik Mohamed Din said on Wednesday.
Asked at a stock market function when T-plus-5, meaning five settlement days from the day of transaction, would replace the current T-plus-7 period, he said: "August 18".
The change to T-plus-5 moves payment for share transactions two days earlier from T-plus-7.
Officials have said that a shorter settlement will promote liquidity, reduce risks and improve efficiency in the Kuala Lumpur share market.

Asked if Malaysia's stock market would immediately switch to an even shorter settlement period of T-plus-three as has been rumoured in the past, Securities Commission chairman Munir Abdul Majid said: "No, it's not true."
He added: "We want to establish T-plus-5 (first)".
The United States and other developed markets operate on T-plus-3 or less, and Malaysia's planned shorter settlement period is partly to bring its market in line with international standards.
